notes: Primary ask: throughput guarantees tied to token/sec not just GPU count - want min tokens/sec for contract enforcement.
Arkstone insists on clear concurrency caps per customer session (300 concurrent active chats target).
They want burst policy spelled out: acceptable bursts up to 2x sustained capacity for at most 10 minutes, >10 minutes triggers throttling and credit/backfill options.
POC observations: quantized model variant (8-bit) reduces cost but increases variance in p95; Arkstone prefers predictable latency over marginal cost savings.
Customer quote (CPO): 'We will pay for predictability — if you give us a numeric tokens/sec SLO and predictable throttles, we can commit.'
Negotiation pressure: procurement pushes for credits for missed tokens/sec SLA, legal wants caps on credit liability (max 25% ARR).
Routing/fallback requirement: automatic fallback to lower-cost model variant on capacity shortage but must preserve response shape and hallucination controls.
Network/residency: primary region us-east-1; cross-region fallback to us-west-2 allowed only with customer opt-in and data residency flagging.
sales_summary: Enterprise FS customer evaluating Redwood Dedicated. Focused on guaranteed throughput (min tokens/sec), deterministic concurrency caps, and explicit burst behavior. Cost-sensitive but willing to trade unit price for firm SLOs. Key decision hinges on SLA language for sustained tokens/sec, defined throttling behavior, and maximum financial liability for missed SLOs.
technical_requirements: Sustained min tokens/sec: 120,000 tokens/sec across a 3-hour peak window; concurrency cap: 300 active sessions; burst policy: up to 2x sustained for 10 minutes with graceful throttling after; required p95 latency target: <250ms for chat generation at 512-token responses; model variants: base LLM (gpt-mid) + quantized fallback; prefix/KV caching mandatory; must support per-route telemetry and token accounting.
poC_plan: Week 0: sign NDA + initial config. Week 1: deploy 2x80GB dedicated pool in us-east-1. Week 2: synthetic workload run to validate sustained tokens/sec. Week 3: mixed workload run (rerank + chat) and SLA measurement. Week 4: SLA negotiation + pricing addendum.
commercial_notes: Proposed commercial: reserved capacity commit 12 months; base price + burst overage per 10k tokens. Legal requests cap on total SLA credits and explicit definition of measurement window. Procurement wants ability to scale down at 6 months with 30% penalty.
